description: Canonical, SDK-independent coverage vectors for experimental principal-level reporting subscriptions: for each input, every period the seller owes. Each case gives the buyer-side input and either the exact owed periods (expected, one row per buy, resolved offering, and period, and expected_obligations, the same rows grouped the way obligations carry them) or the input error (expected_error). Every expected row is derived from the spec text cited in spec_refs. scripts/reference/reporting-coverage is a brute-force reference model, written from the same text, that reproduces every case; tests/reporting-subscription-coverage-vectors.test.cjs runs it. Each case validates against case.schema.json in this directory. Like the feature, the vectors are experimental and change with it.

tzdata.stability: Expected rows are derived with this IANA tzdata release. Each case lists the zones its rows depend on in timezones. Dates are chosen where releases 2026b through 2026f agree, so an implementation on any of them reproduces every case; compare against this release when they differ.

conventions.instants: Every timestamp is an RFC 3339 instant and may carry fractional seconds or a non-Z offset. Compare instants, never strings. Expected rows write instants in Z form, with fractional seconds only when they are non-zero. Inputs carry at most millisecond precision.
conventions.rows: expected has one row per (media buy, resolved offering, owed period), ordered by period_start, then subscription_version, then offering_id and media_buy_id in byte order. subscription_id, account_id, and report_definition_id are omitted: they are input.subscription_id, input.account.account_id, and the offering's report_definition_id. A billing cutover stub row, and its obligation, carry stub: true.
conventions.obligations: expected_obligations groups expected by subscription_version, offering_id, period_start, and period_end, with media_buy_ids sorted in byte order, the obligation's frozen media_buy_ids. Ordered by period_start, then subscription_version, then offering_id in byte order.
conventions.now: Only resolved periods are expected: those whose period_end is at or before input.now.
conventions.input: The input is what the buyer holds: its subscription versions as the get_principal readback shows them, the account's grants and timezone, the buys it can see through get_media_buys, the seller's offerings, and this subscription's get_reporting_status subscription_coverage entry for the account. case.schema.json describes each field.
conventions.expected_error: When the input cannot determine coverage, expected_error gives the error code and detail an SDK raises, from error-codes.json in this directory (COVERAGE_INPUT_INCOMPLETE or COVERAGE_INPUT_INVALID). wire_valid is false when the input also fails AdCP schema validation.
conventions.vocabularies: error-codes.json freezes the error codes SDKs raise for subscriptions and coverage; reason-codes.json freezes the reasons a period is or is not owed. Both SDKs use them verbatim.

cases.name: baseline
cases.rule: adcp#8593: the start bound is the first boundary at or after max(accepted_at 11-01T12, authorized_at 10-01) = 11-02; owed are the periods from it that end after confirmed_at 11-02T15 and overlap the flight (11-03 on), through the period containing the stop time.

cases.name: mid-period confirmed_at
cases.rule: adcp#8593: confirmed_at 11-03T10 falls inside the first flight day. That period ends after confirmed_at, so it is owed in full; confirmed_at no longer moves the start to the next boundary.

cases.name: confirmed long before the flight
cases.rule: A buy confirmed before accepted_at with a later start owes nothing before start_time.

cases.name: stop time mid-period is owed in full
cases.rule: end_time 11-05T12 is inside the 11-05 period, which is owed in full: periods are never clipped.

cases.name: cancellation mid-flight
cases.rule: canceled_at 11-05T06 is the stop time (earlier than end_time 11-10); its period is owed and none after.

cases.name: cancellation notice period is owed through the delivery stop
cases.rule: adcp#8617: canceled_at 11-05T06 records the cancellation, but the seller delivers through a notice period until cancellation_effective_at 11-07T00, the delivery stop. The stop time is the earliest of end_time, the delivery stop, and completed_at, so periods through 11-06 are owed; canceled_at alone would have stopped them at the period containing it.

cases.name: early completion on a boundary
cases.rule: completed_at 11-04T00 stops the flight on a boundary: the 11-04 period does not overlap [start, stop).

cases.name: flight extension adds only unresolved periods
cases.rule: end_time moved 11-06 -> 11-08 at 11-07T12. The 11-06 period resolved at 11-07T00 under the old end_time and is never owed retroactively; 11-07 resolves after the extension.

cases.name: reinstatement after cancellation
cases.rule: Canceled at 11-04T12, reinstated at 11-06T12. 11-05 resolved while canceled and stays unowed; 11-06 onward resolve after reinstatement.

cases.name: only resolved periods are returned
cases.rule: With now at 11-05T12, the 11-05 period has not ended.

cases.name: unconfirmed buy
cases.rule: A buy with confirmed_at null is not covered.

cases.name: late authorization (authorized_at refinement)
cases.rule: authorized_at 11-04T10 is the latest of the three start terms: coverage starts at 11-05.

cases.name: new subscription version, aligned schedules
cases.rule: v2 accepted 11-04T12. v1 owes periods starting before T in full (11-03, 11-04); E = 11-05 and v2 owes from there. Contiguous, nothing twice.

cases.name: new subscription version, misaligned boundaries
cases.rule: v1 resolves a UTC day offering, v2 (alignment account_timezone) a New York day offering. v1 owes UTC days starting before 11-04T12 (E = 11-05T00Z); v2 owes New York days starting at or after E, the first being 11-05T05Z. 11-05T00Z-05Z is owed under neither.

cases.name: billing cutover owes a stub
cases.rule: adcp#8617: v1 resolves a UTC-day billing offering, v2 (accepted 11-04T12Z, alignment account_timezone) a New York-day one. v1 owes UTC days starting before T, through E = 11-05T00Z. On a billing feed the stretch to the first New York boundary is owed as one stub period [11-05T00Z, 11-05T05Z), flagged stub; New York days follow from 11-05T05Z. Billable time is contiguous.

cases.name: deactivation
cases.rule: deactivated_at 11-04T12: the 11-04 period started before it and stays owed in full; nothing later.

cases.name: deactivation then reactivation in place
cases.rule: Readback inactive_intervals [11-04T12, 11-06T12): a cutover out at 11-04T12 and a fresh start at the first boundary at or after 11-06T12 (11-07).

cases.name: account new in a later version
cases.rule: v1 names another account; v2 (all accounts, accepted 11-04T12) brings acct_1 in under the ordinary start rule: 11-05.

cases.name: excluded_by_buyer scope
cases.rule: An all-accounts subscription that lists the account in exclude_account_ids covers nothing for it.

cases.name: operator_domains scope
cases.rule: operator_domains keeps only accounts whose operator is listed.

cases.name: revocation
cases.rule: unauthorized_at 11-05T06: periods starting at or after the last boundary at or before it (11-05) are not owed. 11-03 and 11-04 ended before it and stay owed (withheld until re-grant if undelivered).

cases.name: re-grant without backfill
cases.rule: Re-granted 11-06T18 within status_retention_days: the gap [11-05, 11-07) is not owed; coverage resumes at 11-07 and the earlier periods stay owed.

cases.name: re-grant with backfill_on_regrant
cases.rule: With backfill_on_regrant no gap is recorded and every period in the revoked interval stays owed.

cases.name: re-grant after the unauthorized entry expired
cases.rule: status_retention_days 1: the entry expired at 11-06T06, so the 11-06T18 re-grant is a fresh start from authorized_at (11-07) and backfill does not apply.

cases.name: seller gaps also remove periods
cases.rule: A gaps[] entry the seller published removes the periods starting in [from, until), like an exception.

cases.name: exceptions only remove periods
cases.rule: Account-level capacity [11-04, 11-06) removes 11-04 and 11-05 for every buy; a buy-level offering_unsupported removes mb_2 from 11-03; a package_ids entry removes packages, not periods; an exception before coverage adds nothing.

cases.name: max_accounts capacity exception
cases.rule: Beyond subscriptions.max_accounts the seller records an open account-level capacity exception; nothing is owed from its from.

cases.name: precedence over an account-level configuration
cases.rule: The caller's own sync_accounts configuration takes the account from 11-04 to 11-05 (overridden), after which replace_account_configs hands it back.

cases.name: match exact (default with dimensions)
cases.rule: exact [package] picks the offering whose dimension set equals it; package x device (unmapped device) is distinct.

cases.name: match exact with no equal offering
cases.rule: exact [package] against package x creative, package x country and package x device (unmapped) resolves nothing: offering_unsupported, no periods.

cases.name: match exact on two dimensions
cases.rule: exact [package, country] picks package x country.

cases.name: match finest
cases.rule: finest [package] picks the most mapped dimensions among offerings including package; package x creative and package x country tie at two, so the lowest offering_id in byte order wins.

cases.name: match defaults to finest without dimensions
cases.rule: No dimensions: match defaults to finest over every candidate.

cases.name: match all
cases.rule: all [package] picks every offering including package, each owed its own periods (package x device included: it includes package).

cases.name: product eligibility gates candidates
cases.rule: Only offerings in the product's reporting_delivery_offering_ids are candidates; a package with none leaves the buy covered by its other packages.

cases.name: finality, purpose and duration must match
cases.rule: An offering advertising only snapshot finality, another feed_purpose, or another period_duration is never a candidate.

cases.name: a newly available offering never re-resolves
cases.rule: finest [package]: the (buy, version) pair resolves at the later of accepted_at (11-01T12) and confirmed_at (11-02T15), when only package is available. package x creative becomes available at 11-04T12, but an offering added later never re-resolves the pair, so package owes every period of the flight.
cases.changed_from_origin: Re-ruled for 3.3.0-beta.3 (adcp#8619): resolution is fixed per (buy, version) when the pair first resolves, so package x creative becoming available at 11-04T12 no longer changes it. The origin case expected a resolution change at that instant.

cases.name: withdrawal of the resolved offering is a cutover
cases.rule: finest [package]: package x creative is available throughout and wins at resolution. It is withdrawn at 11-04T12, the one resolution change within a version: the package re-resolves to package, and the cutover hands off at E = 11-05. package x creative owes 11-03 and 11-04; package owes from 11-05.

cases.name: account timezone
cases.rule: An account_timezone offering uses New York midnights (05:00Z in November). accepted_at 11-01T12Z: first boundary 11-02T05Z. The 11-02T05Z day contains confirmed_at 11-02T15Z and overlaps the flight from 11-03T00Z, so it is owed (adcp#8593).

cases.name: account timezone across a DST change
cases.rule: New York falls back on 2026-11-01: the 11-01 local day is 25 hours, 04:00Z to 05:00Z the next day.

cases.name: account timezone change is a cutover
cases.rule: The account moves to Los Angeles (account.timezone is the current zone); timezone_cutovers.effective_at 11-05T05Z is E and previous_timezone New York governs before it. New York days starting before E are owed, then Los Angeles days from the first boundary at or after it (11-05T08Z). 05Z-08Z is owed under neither.

cases.name: period_timezone override
cases.rule: A single-account subscription with period_timezone Asia/Tokyo uses Tokyo midnights (15:00Z). confirmed_at 11-02T15Z is itself a boundary, so the period ending at it is not owed and the one starting at it is.

cases.name: hourly periods are never clipped
cases.rule: Flight 10:30-13:15, confirmed 10:20: the 10:00 period ends after confirmed_at and overlaps the flight, so it is owed in full (adcp#8593), and the 13:00 period containing the stop is owed in full.

cases.name: monthly billing cycle
cases.changed_from_origin: managed offerings completed to validate against reporting-delivery-offering.json (method.provider and method.format; canonicalization fields for consumer_receipt); coverage is unchanged
cases.rule: A fixed billing_cycle anchored at New York midnight: month boundaries move between 04:00Z (EDT) and 05:00Z (EST). The month containing the stop is owed in full.

cases.name: ASAP buy confirmed mid-day owes the confirmation day
cases.rule: adcp#8593: an ASAP buy starts when it is confirmed, 11-03T14:30Z. The 11-03 period ends after confirmed_at and overlaps the flight, so it is owed in full.

cases.name: monthly billing buy confirmed on the 12th owes that month
cases.changed_from_origin: managed offerings completed to validate against reporting-delivery-offering.json (method.provider and method.format; canonicalization fields for consumer_receipt); coverage is unchanged
cases.rule: adcp#8593: the version was accepted 10-15, so the start bound is the November boundary (11-01T04Z). The buy is confirmed and starts on 11-12; the November month ends after confirmed_at and overlaps the flight, so it is owed in full rather than starting in December.

cases.name: destination selects managed offerings only
cases.changed_from_origin: managed offerings completed to validate against reporting-delivery-offering.json (method.provider and method.format; canonicalization fields for consumer_receipt); coverage is unchanged
cases.rule: With a destination only offerings whose method matches its pattern and transport are candidates; without one only Core (method-less) offerings are.

cases.name: multiple buys group into obligations
cases.rule: Each (buy, offering) pair is owed its own periods; obligations group them by period with frozen media_buy_ids. mb_0, confirmed 11-03T12, is owed the 11-03 period it was confirmed in (adcp#8593).

cases.name: timezone cutover scoped to one offering
cases.rule: A timezone_cutovers entry with offering_id applies to that offering only; an offering with no applicable entry uses account.timezone (Los Angeles) throughout.

cases.name: gap scoped to one offering
cases.rule: A gaps[] entry with offering_id removes only that offering's periods; an entry without offering_id applies to every offering.

cases.name: match exact without dimensions
cases.rule: exact with no dimensions: every candidate qualifies and the lowest offering_id in byte order wins.

cases.name: period_timezone never matches an account-resolved source_timezone offering
cases.rule: A source_timezone offering matches a period_timezone override only when its published period_timezone equals it; an account_resolved offering publishes none.

cases.name: period_timezone matches a fixed source_timezone offering in the same zone
cases.rule: A fixed source_timezone offering publishing America/New_York matches a New York override and keeps its own boundaries (05:00Z in November).

cases.name: a utc offering matches only UTC or Etc/UTC
cases.rule: period_timezone GMT is not one of the UTC aliases core/reporting-subscription.json names, so the utc offering does not match.

cases.name: empty flight: canceled before start_time
cases.rule: canceled_at 11-05T02 is before start_time 11-05T06: the flight [start, stop) is empty and overlaps nothing, though the 11-05 period contains both instants.

cases.name: empty flight: stop equal to start
cases.rule: A zero-length flight (end_time equal to start_time at 11-03T12) is empty and overlaps nothing.

cases.name: two cutovers inside one period
cases.rule: v2 (11-04T12Z) switches to a Tokyo period_timezone and v3 (11-04T13Z) changes nothing else. v1 owes its New York day starting 11-04T05Z, through 11-05T05Z. v2 owes from that E and starts nothing before 13Z. v3 must carry v2's own start forward: it owes Tokyo days from the first boundary at or after 11-05T05Z (11-05T15Z), never the overlapping 11-04T15Z.

cases.name: simultaneous version and timezone change at the same T
cases.rule: v2 is accepted at 11-05T05Z, exactly the timezone cutover effective_at (a New York boundary). v1 owes New York days starting before it; v2 owes Los Angeles days from the first boundary at or after it (11-05T08Z).

cases.name: billing cycle anchored on the 31st clamps to month end
cases.changed_from_origin: managed offerings completed to validate against reporting-delivery-offering.json (method.provider and method.format; canonicalization fields for consumer_receipt); coverage is unchanged
cases.rule: P1M from 2026-01-31 New York midnight: the 31st clamps to Feb 28 and returns to the 31st in March (a clamped February boundary does not shift the anchor day).

cases.name: billing cycle anchored on February 29
cases.changed_from_origin: managed offerings completed to validate against reporting-delivery-offering.json (method.provider and method.format; canonicalization fields for consumer_receipt); coverage is unchanged
cases.rule: P1Y from 2024-02-29T00:00Z: non-leap years clamp to Feb 28 and 2028 returns to Feb 29.

cases.name: DST fold at midnight (America/Santiago)
cases.rule: Chile falls back at 24:00 on 2026-04-04 to 23:00, so April 4 is a 25-hour local day; local midnight April 5 occurs once, at 04:00Z.

cases.name: DST gap at midnight (America/Santiago)
cases.rule: Chile springs forward at 24:00 on 2026-09-05 to 01:00: local midnight September 6 does not exist and the boundary advances by the gap to 04:00Z, so September 6 is a 23-hour local day.

cases.name: zero-length period on a skipped civil date (Pacific/Apia)
cases.rule: Samoa skipped 2011-12-30: that local day has zero length (its midnight and the next coincide at 10:00Z) and is never owed; the surrounding days are.

cases.name: PT24H under a local alignment restarts at local midnight (#8588)
cases.rule: Under account_timezone a duration of only hours restarts at each local midnight (adcp#8588), so PT24H in New York across the 2026-03-08 spring-forward has a 23-hour period, exactly like P1D.

cases.name: PT24H and P1D under utc are the same days
cases.rule: UTC has no DST, so PT24H and P1D yield identical boundaries under utc alignment.

cases.name: sub-daily local periods start on the local hour (Asia/Singapore)
cases.rule: adcp#8588: hourly periods under account_timezone are local wall-clock hours counted from each local midnight, not 1970 offsets (Singapore was +07:30 in 1970). confirmed_at 00:05Z falls in the 00:00Z (08:00 local) hour, which ends after it and overlaps the flight, so it is owed (adcp#8593).

cases.name: sub-daily local periods on a 25-hour day (America/New_York fall-back)
cases.rule: adcp#8588: the repeated 01:00 yields one boundary per offset, so 2026-11-01 in New York has 25 hourly periods.

cases.name: re-grant chain of three grants without backfill
cases.rule: Revoked 11-04T06 and re-granted 11-05T18, revoked 11-07T06 and re-granted 11-08T18, all inside retention: one chain with gaps [11-04, 11-06) and [11-07, 11-09).

cases.name: re-grant chain of three grants with backfill_on_regrant
cases.rule: The same chain with backfill_on_regrant: no gap, every period owed.

cases.name: re-grant seen only through the chain-start authorized_at
cases.rule: The wire keeps authorized_at at the chain start after a re-grant inside retention (adcp#8585), so the buyer lists the continuation with that value; the seller's gaps[] says which periods the interruption removed.

cases.name: two authorization chains
cases.rule: Revoked 11-04T06; re-granted 11-10 after retention (1 day) expired, a new chain from 11-10; revoked again 11-12T06.

cases.name: match all adds an offering on a different alignment
cases.rule: v2 (11-04T12Z) moves from exact to all and adds a New York offering. The UTC offering continues (E = 11-05T00Z); the New York offering is new and starts at the latest outgoing end, so its first period is 11-05T05Z and 00Z-05Z is owed by neither.

cases.name: version change exactly on a boundary
cases.rule: v2 accepted at 11-05T00Z, itself a boundary: E is T, v1 owes 11-03 and 11-04, v2 from 11-05.

cases.name: reactivation exactly on a boundary
cases.rule: Inactive [11-04T12, 11-06T00): 11-04 started before deactivation and stays owed; coverage resumes at 11-06 itself.

cases.name: inactive interval spanning a version change
cases.rule: Deactivated under v1 at 11-04T12, v2 accepted while inactive at 11-05T12, reactivated 11-06T12: v1 owes 11-03 and 11-04, v2 starts fresh at 11-07.

cases.name: reactivation after a schedule change never owes twice
cases.rule: 3.3.0-beta.3: v1 resolves a UTC day offering and is deactivated at 11-04T12Z, so its 11-04T00Z day stays owed through 11-05T00Z. While inactive, v2 is accepted at 11-04T13Z with alignment account_timezone in Tokyo (midnight 15:00Z), and the subscription is reactivated at 11-04T14Z. Coverage resumes at the first boundary at or after the later of the reactivation instant and the end of the last period owed before deactivation (11-05T00Z): 11-05T15Z. The fresh start alone would have owed the Tokyo day from 11-04T15Z, overlapping the owed UTC day.

cases.name: exception bounds between boundaries
cases.rule: capacity [11-04T12, 11-06T12) removes the periods whose start is in it, 11-05 and 11-06; 11-04 started before from and stays owed.

cases.name: finest tie in byte order (B before a)
cases.rule: Two offerings tie at two mapped dimensions; byte order puts uppercase B (0x42) before lowercase a (0x61), unlike locale order.

cases.name: unknown dimension values parse and match only where published
cases.rule: The dimension vocabulary is extensible: an offering may publish placement, and a selector naming it matches that offering. A value no offering publishes (audience_segment) matches nothing.

cases.name: an unknown selector dimension no offering publishes matches nothing
cases.rule: A selector naming a value the seller does not map matches no offering.

cases.name: numeric offset timezone is refused
cases.changed_from_origin: offering is account_timezone-aligned instead of utc-aligned
cases.rule: iana_timezone: an account_timezone offering reads its boundaries in the account timezone, and +05:00 is a numeric offset, not an IANA zone, so it defines no DST rules. Changed from the adcp-client#3505 table, whose offering was utc-aligned: a utc schedule never reads the account timezone, so its periods are derivable and the refusal did not follow from the coverage rule.

cases.name: account_timezone offering requires the account timezone
cases.rule: Boundaries cannot be derived without the account timezone.

cases.name: a timezone cutover without previous_timezone is refused
cases.rule: Sellers MUST include previous_timezone: account.timezone already shows the new zone, so the old schedule cannot be recovered without it.

cases.name: an offering without standard_dimensions cannot be resolved
cases.rule: Sellers advertising subscriptions MUST publish standard_dimensions on every offering; matching never guesses.

cases.name: re-grant requires status_retention_days
cases.rule: Whether a re-grant continues coverage depends on the retention window.

cases.name: DST gap at midnight (America/Havana)
cases.rule: Cuba springs forward at 00:00 standard time on 2026-03-08 (Rule Cuba Mar Sun>=8 0:00s). Local midnight March 8 does not exist, so the boundary advances by the one-hour gap to 01:00 CDT, 05:00Z. March 7 is a 24-hour local day (05:00Z to 05:00Z) and March 8 a 23-hour one (05:00Z to 04:00Z).

cases.name: Sub-daily local periods on a day whose midnight does not exist (America/Havana)
cases.rule: adcp#8588: hourly boundaries are the instants whose local wall time is a whole hour, and a wall time that does not exist yields no boundary. 00:00 on 2026-03-08 does not exist in Havana; 01:00 CDT (05:00Z) is the first boundary of the day, so March 8 has 23 hourly periods, each one hour long.

cases.name: havana PT24H equals P1D when midnight does not exist
cases.rule: Each local date's day start, its first instant, is always a boundary of a sub-daily local schedule (3.3.0-beta.3). Havana springs forward at 00:00 on 2026-03-08, so March 8 starts at 01:00 CDT (05:00Z). PT24H has its boundary there, exactly like P1D: March 7 is 24 hours and March 8 is 23. Under the earlier reading the nonexistent midnight yielded no boundary and PT24H had a 47-hour period.

cases.name: havana PT2H nests in the day
cases.rule: The day start is a boundary of every sub-daily local schedule, so local days nest in two-hour periods even when midnight does not exist. On 2026-03-08 in Havana, 00:00 does not exist and the day starts at 01:00 CDT (05:00Z): the PT2H periods are 05:00Z-06:00Z (one hour, from the day start to 02:00 CDT) and then two-hour periods from 06:00Z. March 7 ends at 05:00Z with 22:00-24:00 CST (03:00Z-05:00Z).

cases.name: DST fold at midnight: the earlier offset (America/Havana)
cases.rule: Cuba fell back at 00:00 standard time on 2025-11-02 (01:00 CDT became 00:00 CST), so local midnight November 2 occurred twice, at 04:00Z and 05:00Z. An ambiguous local boundary uses the earlier offset: November 2 starts at 04:00Z and is a 25-hour local day, ending at 05:00Z on November 3. Chosen in 2025 because tzdata 2026f removed Cuba's 2026-11-01 fall-back; no release from 2026b through 2026f differs on these instants.

cases.name: Sub-daily local periods when midnight repeats (America/Havana)
cases.rule: adcp#8588: a repeated wall time yields one boundary per offset. On 2025-11-02 in Havana 00:00 occurs at 04:00Z (CDT) and again at 05:00Z (CST), so both are boundaries and the 25-hour local day has 25 hourly periods.

cases.name: DST gap at midnight (Africa/Cairo)
cases.rule: Egypt springs forward at 00:00 on the last Friday of April (Rule Egypt Apr lastFri 0:00): 2025-04-25 00:00 EET does not exist and advances by the gap to 01:00 EEST, 22:00Z on April 24. April 24 is 24 hours (22:00Z to 22:00Z) and April 25 is 23 (22:00Z to 21:00Z).

cases.name: DST fold at 24:00 (Africa/Cairo)
cases.rule: Egypt falls back at 24:00 on the last Thursday of October (Rule Egypt Oct lastThu 24:00): on 2025-10-30 at 21:00Z the clock reads 24:00 EEST and returns to 23:00 EET. The repeated hour is 23:00 on October 30, so October 31 00:00 occurs once (22:00Z) and October 30 is a 25-hour local day, 21:00Z on October 29 to 22:00Z on October 30.

cases.name: Sub-daily local periods across a 30-minute spring-forward (Australia/Lord_Howe)
cases.rule: adcp#8588: hourly periods start on the local hour. Lord Howe moves from +10:30 to +11 at 02:00 on 2025-10-05, skipping 02:00-02:30, so wall 02:00 does not exist and yields no boundary. The day has 23 boundaries and 23 periods; the one from 01:00 (14:30Z) to 03:00 (16:00Z) lasts 90 minutes. The local day is 23.5 hours.

cases.name: Sub-daily local periods across a 30-minute fall-back (Australia/Lord_Howe)
cases.rule: Lord Howe returns from +11 to +10:30 at 02:00 on 2026-04-05: at 15:00Z the clock reads 02:00 and goes back to 01:30. Only 01:30-02:00 repeats, so every whole hour occurs once: 24 boundaries and 24 periods, the one from 01:00 (14:00Z) to 02:00 (15:30Z) lasting 90 minutes. The local day is 24.5 hours.

cases.name: A repeated half hour yields one boundary per offset (Australia/Lord_Howe)
cases.rule: With PT30M, wall 01:30 on 2026-04-05 occurs at 14:30Z (+11) and again at 15:00Z (+10:30); both are boundaries. The four half-hour periods from 14:00Z to 16:00Z are each 30 minutes long.

cases.name: Sub-daily local periods at a +05:45 offset (Asia/Kathmandu)
cases.rule: adcp#8588: local hours in Kathmandu (+05:45) start at 15 minutes past each UTC hour, while a utc-aligned hourly offering starts on the UTC hour. match all resolves both offerings and each is owed its own periods: local hours from 23:15Z (the one containing the 00:00Z flight start) through the one containing the 03:00Z stop, and UTC hours 00:00Z to 03:00Z.

cases.name: utc sub-daily periods count from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z
cases.rule: utc alignment uses 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as interval zero and the sub-daily local rule does not apply to it, so PT7H boundaries are multiples of seven hours since the epoch, not since midnight: 2026-11-03T00:00Z is 498240 hours after the epoch, one past a multiple of seven, so boundaries fall at 23:00Z, 06:00Z, 13:00Z and 20:00Z.

cases.name: Billing cycle anchored on the 31st across 30-day months
cases.rule: Month addition preserves the anchor day and clamps to the target month's last day, computed from the anchor for each ordinal: March 31, April 30 (clamped), May 31 (back to the 31st, not April 30 plus one month), June 30, July 31.

cases.name: Quarterly billing cycle anchored on October 31 in New York
cases.rule: P3M from 2025-10-31 00:00 New York: January 31, April 30 (clamped), July 31, October 31. Each is local midnight, so the UTC instant moves between 04:00Z (EDT) and 05:00Z (EST, January 31).

cases.name: Weekly utc periods (P7D) start on Thursdays
cases.rule: The schedule pattern has no W designator, so a week is P7D. utc alignment counts from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, a Thursday, so every utc week starts on a Thursday: 2026-11-05, 11-12 and 11-19 cover a Monday-to-Monday flight.

cases.name: Weekly local periods (P7D) across a fall-back
cases.rule: Under account_timezone the origin is local midnight on 1970-01-01, a Thursday, and days are civil days: the week from Thursday 2026-10-29 00:00 EDT (04:00Z) to Thursday 2026-11-05 00:00 EST (05:00Z) is 7 days and 1 hour.

cases.name: P1W is not a schedule period_duration
cases.rule: The period_duration pattern in core/reporting-schedule.json and the selector allows Y, M and D date components and no W designator; a week is P7D. A P1W selector fails schema validation and cannot be resolved.

cases.name: Yearly local periods (P1Y) are calendar years
cases.rule: Under account_timezone, P1Y from local midnight on 1970-01-01 gives January 1 local midnight each year (05:00Z in New York). Accepted 2025-12-01, the first owed year starts 2026-01-01; a flight into 2027 owes 2027 in full.

cases.name: A local sub-daily duration that does not divide 24 hours is refused
cases.rule: period_generation: with account_timezone, source_timezone, or billing_cycle alignment, a period_duration made only of hours, minutes, and seconds MUST divide 24 hours. PT7H does not.

cases.name: A local alignment cannot mix date and time components
cases.rule: period_generation: "With those alignments a period_duration cannot mix date and time components." P1DT12H under account_timezone is refused.

cases.name: sub-daily billing cycle is refused
cases.rule: period_generation (3.3.0-beta.3): billing_cycle alignment requires a period_duration with a date component. A sub-daily duration restarts at each local midnight, so the anchor would have no effect; PT1H under billing_cycle is refused, and the reporting-schedule schema rejects it.

cases.name: Fractional seconds and non-Z offsets are instants
cases.rule: Every timestamp is an RFC 3339 instant; compare instants, never strings. accepted_at 2026-11-01T19:00:00.001-05:00 is one millisecond after the 11-02T00:00Z boundary, so the first owed boundary is 11-03. authorized_at, confirmed_at, the flight and now use +05:30, +01:00, -05:00 and +09:00 offsets and fractional seconds; the flight is 11-02T00:00Z to 11-05T00:00Z and now is 11-06T00:00Z. Expected instants are written in Z form.

cases.name: Confirmed one millisecond before a boundary owes the period containing it
cases.rule: adcp#8593: a period is owed when it ends after confirmed_at. confirmed_at 10:59:59.999Z is inside the 10:00Z hour, which ends after it and overlaps the 10:30Z flight start, so it is owed in full.

cases.name: Confirmed exactly on a boundary owes from that boundary
cases.rule: confirmed_at 11:00:00.000+00:00 is a boundary: the 10:00Z hour ends at it, not after it, so it is not owed even though it overlaps the flight; 11:00Z and 12:00Z are.

cases.name: A buy confirmed after its stop owes only a period that ends after confirmation
cases.rule: mb_1 stops at 11-05T12 and is confirmed at 11-05T06: only the 11-05 period both ends after confirmed_at and overlaps the flight. mb_2 has the same flight and is confirmed at 11-06T01, after the period containing its stop ended, so it owes nothing.

cases.name: Extending an empty flight never owes the periods resolved while it was empty
cases.rule: Until 11-04T12 the flight was empty (start_time equal to end_time, 11-03T00), so the 11-03 period, resolved at 11-04T00, overlapped nothing. The update at 11-04T12 sets end_time 11-07; periods resolved after it (11-04, 11-05, 11-06) use the new flight and are owed, and 11-03 never becomes owed retroactively.

cases.name: Each package resolves the selector against its own product
cases.rule: The seller resolves the selector separately for each buy's products. Under finest [package], pkg_1's product lists package and package x creative and resolves package x creative; pkg_2's product lists only package and resolves it. The buy is covered by both, and each (buy, resolved offering) pair is owed its own periods.

cases.name: Reactivation and a new version at the same instant
cases.rule: Deactivated at 11-04T12 under v1; v2 is accepted and the subscription reactivated at the same instant, 11-05T12. v1 owes the periods that started before the deactivation (11-03, 11-04). Reactivation is a fresh start, so v2 owes from the first boundary at or after 11-05T12 (11-06), and nothing that started while inactive.

cases.name: A new version deactivated at the instant it is accepted
cases.rule: v2 is accepted at 11-04T12 with active false, deactivated_at 11-04T12. v1 is outgoing at T and owes the periods that start before it (11-03, 11-04); deactivation has no incoming schedule, so v2 owes nothing.

cases.name: A revocation and a new version at the same instant
cases.rule: Authority ends at 11-04T12, the instant v2 is accepted, and returns at 11-05T18 inside retention without backfill. v1 owes the periods starting before T, but the 11-04 period ends after unauthorized_at and falls in the gap [11-04, 11-06); 11-03 stays owed. v2 owes from E = 11-05 except the gap, so from 11-06.

cases.name: Four grants: two chains, each with an interruption, without backfill
cases.rule: status_retention_days 2. The 11-04T00 re-grant is before 11-03T06 + 2 days and continues the first chain: gap [11-03, 11-04). The 11-07T12 re-grant is exactly 11-05T12 + 2 days, not before it, so the entry has expired and a new chain starts at 11-07T12 (first owed boundary 11-08); 11-05 to 11-07 end after the first chain's final unauthorized_at and start before the new chain. The 11-10T00 re-grant continues the second chain: gap [11-09, 11-10).

cases.name: Four grants: two chains, each with an interruption, with backfill_on_regrant
cases.rule: The same grants with backfill_on_regrant: the interruptions inside each chain record no gap, so 11-03 and 11-09 are owed. Backfill never bridges two chains: 11-05 to 11-07 stay unowed.

cases.name: max_accounts capacity exception per offering on different boundaries
cases.rule: Beyond subscriptions.max_accounts the seller excludes the account with reason capacity from 11-04T12 until it is served again at 11-06T12. Under match all the covered offerings have different boundaries, so the seller lists one entry per offering_id with that offering's E instants: UTC days [11-05T00, 11-07T00) and New York days [11-05T05, 11-07T05). Each removes only its own offering's periods.

cases.name: An account-resolved source_timezone offering needs the seller-resolved zone
cases.rule: A source_timezone offering with period_timezone_policy account_resolved publishes no zone; the seller resolves the account's upstream reporting timezone and echoes it as the obligation's period.source_timezone. Without that value the boundaries cannot be derived.
